chunks: 5441 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Zurarah, who said:

I asked him about a man who died while owing a debt equal to the price of his shroud. He said: "What he left behind should be used for the price of his shroud, unless some people undertake it for him, then they shroud him, and what he owed is paid from what he left behind."

key_terms.ثَمَنِ كَفَنِهِ: The cost of the deceased's shroud.
key_terms.دَيْنٌ: A debt owed by the deceased.
key_terms.فَيُكَفِّنُونَهُ: They provide him with a shroud.
key_terms.مَا تَرَكَ: The property or estate left behind by the deceased.
key_terms.يُقْضَى مَا عَلَيْهِ: What he owes is paid off.

ai.seo_question: If a deceased person leaves only enough wealth for his shroud, is the money used for the shroud first or to pay his debt?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on the estate of a deceased person whose remaining wealth is only enough to cover the cost of his shroud. The estate is first used for the shroud, unless others voluntarily provide it, in which case the estate is used to settle the deceased's debt.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.5441 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Riʾab from Zurarah, who said:
I asked Imam (as) about a man who died while owing a debt equal to the price of his shroud.

Imam (as) said: "What he left behind should be used for the price of his shroud unless some people choose to contribute and provide his shroud. In that case, his debt should be paid off from what he left behind."
